newsitem.title: UK: Spanish debt, JGBs top gainers in week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Spanish debt, JGBs top gainers in week - Salomon.

text.p: Spanish and Japanese bonds turned in modest gains in the latest week, leading the way for a mixed market, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.

Spanish Bonos made a 0.44 percent return in peseta terms in the week to Thursday. Analysts said Bonos benefit from positive fundamentals and have outperformed other high yielding markets despite worries about the single European currency process.
Yields of Japanese government bonds (JGBs) fell to record lows earlier in the week, bolstered by talk of capital repatriation and nearly non-existent inflationary pressures, analysts said.
JGBs made a 0.43 percent return in yen terms, Salomon said.
The overall world government bond index, which comprises 16 major markets, managed a 0.06 percent gain. U.S. Treasuries similarly made a 0.04 percent return.
The worst performing market was Switzerland, whose bonds made a 0.82 percent loss in the week. This followed a top-performing 0.49 percent return in the previous week.

In U.S. dollar terms, the best market was Australia, which showed a 1.39 percent gain. Most markets registered positive returns for dollar-based investors, with only Britain, Sweden and Japan showing losses.
British gilts lost 0.80 percent, Swedish bonds 0.75 percent and JGBs 0.59 percent in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
